transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

I’m here because I can’t shut my brain off anymore. One thing starts it—like a client not responding—and then within minutes I’m thinking I’ll lose the contract, fall behind on my divorce payments, and never get back into a real leadership role. It just keeps going.
About how long have you been experiencing this kind of constant worrying?
Since I was fired, about thirteen months ago. It really hasn’t let up, even after I found contract work.
Alongside this worry, have you been feeling persistently down, depressed, or sad most days?
I’m not really sure. I know I’ve been stressed and worried constantly, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed feeling sad most days.
Along with this constant worry, do you often feel restless, keyed up, or on edge?

Yes. I feel wound up most of the day, like my shoulders are tight and I’m just waiting for bad news. I pace around the house sometimes, and during calls I’ll be bouncing my leg even when nothing’s actually going on.
Has this worry been affecting your sleep, such as trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or having restless sleep?

Yeah. Most nights I’m lying there replaying interview answers or checking the clock at two or three in the morning. And even when I get what should be enough sleep, I wake up feeling like I was on call all night for a system outage.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports excessive, uncontrollable anxiety and worry across multiple life domains (work, finances, career) lasting for approximately 13 months. Associated symptoms include feeling keyed up/on edge, physical/muscle tension (tight shoulders, pacing, leg bouncing), and significant sleep disturbance (difficulty falling and staying asleep, non-restorative sleep), fulfilling criteria for Generalized Anxiety Disorder.
